lead_headline: Restaurant tracker explodes to 33 active leads as Aspen Baking's sudden collapse reverberates, foreclosure filings slip 33%, and subscriber net swings negative after Sunday's +6 surge.

restaurant.blurb: 8 fresh leads today elevate the active roster to 33 total (15 openings, 18 closures). Monday's bombshell: Aspen Baking Company shuttered March 6 after 30+ years, leaving restaurant clients scrambling mid-acquisition. Openings: Rosie's Ice Cream relocates from Berkeley to Wash Park West's S Pearl corridor, while Wapos Cantina (Boulder chain) debuts in Rosedale's former El Tepehuan space and Mendocino Farms plants its third Denver flag at Union Station. Closures deepen: 303 Ramen fire-sidelined in Regis, New Dragon (13-year Berkeley fixture) dark since late February, both Dairy Queen locations confirmed gone (Regis and Fort Logan). Safeway's November 2025 Aurora closure finally surfaced—regional consolidation's long tail catching up.

foreclosure.blurb: 33 new filings this week—matching last week's filing count but down 33% from two weeks prior's 49, cementing the post-winter cooldown. Aggregate exposure: $11.1M, led by Douglas County's $628K Lumos Lane case. 44 auctions queued for the next seven days. Weld County still commands at 335 active cases, Arapahoe follows at 290. Three consecutive weeks of deceleration confirm the filing frenzy has broken—whether it's sustainable restraint or the calm before spring's traditionally hotter auction season remains the only question mark.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention today holds the 7-day tally at 49 across 14 unique sources—the tracker's entire operational history since last week's launch. Denver Post still owns the leaderboard with 19 citations, Instagram and Hoodline each contribute 6, Facebook matches at 6. Today's lone pickup: Instagram post on Denver Tech Center office building developments. Google News RSS continues as the dominant discovery channel (48 of 49 captures). No week-over-week comparison possible yet—tracker launched into immediate activity, establishing baseline velocity but awaiting next Monday's data to measure true momentum shift.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −1 yesterday (0 new, 1 canceled) snaps Sunday's +6 momentum but leaves March MTD at +7 (+0.8/day), with 90-day cumulative at +72. Past fortnight reveals whipsaw volatility: Feb 24's catastrophic −9 preceded a robust seven-day +8 climb, then early March wobbled with −5 across two days before last weekend's +8 three-day rally. Yesterday's single cancellation reads as noise, not trend reversal. YTD pace of +1.1/day still outpaces March's 0.8 rate—the question is whether Monday's stumble signals renewed churn or just routine turbulence after Sunday's outsized +6 intake.
